messages:
sam k: Quick help please  I had to see a walk-in clinic in Vancouver last night for a sprained wrist. Provider billed me OON and said insurance wouldn't accept because it's outside the US. I have the itemized receipt but no idea how to file. Can People Ops advise?

melissa: Sorry that happened, @sam k. For emergency/urgent care while traveling we do cover after you submit an out-of-network claim. You need: 1) itemized receipt showing services and amounts, 2) provider name, address, NPI or tax ID, 3) ICD/CPT codes if available (they often appear on the receipt).

sam k: I have a PDF receipt (shows service codes and total), provider name and clinic address, and they emailed me a receipt with a case number.

ryan b: Perfect. Next steps: submit via the benefits portal -> Claims -> Submit Out-of-Network. Upload the PDF and add provider tax ID. If the portal rejects Canadian addresses, email claims@redwoodbenefits.example with subject: "OON Claim - International - Sam K - 1783006789" and attach the docs.

people-ops-bot: Note: International out-of-network claims require manual review. Turnaround time is typically 10 business days. For urgent reimbursements, enable "advance payment" in the request or ask People Ops for a one-time emergency advance.

sam k: Filing it now. One question  they charged me in CAD. Do I convert to USD?

melissa: Use the conversion rate on the service date. The claims portal accepts a currency field; if emailing, list USD equivalent and mention the exchange rate source (e.g., xe.com or the bank rate). Include a screenshot of the rate or note the conversion method.

ryan b: Also add bank remittance instructions if you want direct deposit reimbursement. We can reimburse to your US bank. If you need funds sooner, request an emergency advance and we can process within 48 hours subject to approval.

sam k: I requested emergency advance in the portal and attached the receipt. Any other docs they might ask for?

melissa: If the clinic sends an itemized bill (not just a payment receipt), include that. If they only give you a credit card slip, ask for a more detailed statement listing services. Also, keep photos of wrist brace or Rx if they prescribe something; helps with medical necessity review.

people-ops-bot: Case created: PO-7942  International OON claim submitted by Sam K. Status: Pending review. If claim approved, EOB will be emailed; allow 10 business days.

sam k: Clinic asked if Redwood covers imaging pre-authorization for US providers  they want to bill for an X-ray and said pre-auth is required for non-urgent imaging. I couldn't get a pre-auth while overseas. Will that block reimbursement?

ryan b: Good question. For unforeseen urgent imaging done at the time of service, pre-auth is not required for immediate emergency care. If the claim is denied for lack of pre-auth, we'll file an exception with clinical notes. Upload the clinic notes and any imaging report. We handle exceptions for emergency care.

melissa: If you want, we can also draft a provider letter for the clinic to fax us any missing documentation; DM me the clinic fax and I'll request it.

sam k: Thanks  fax is +1-604-555-9876. I'll DM the details. Appreciate the guidance and the advance offer.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: Keep originals of receipts until claim fully processed. For any appeals, include ticket #PO-7942 in subject lines.
